evidence: app/react-router.config.ts:2-4 — config sets only `ssr: true`; no future flags, no unstable options
app/app/routes/not-found.tsx:4 — `data(null, { status: 404 })`; the `data()` utility is stable since v7.2

app/package.json:8-11 — react-router/react-dom/@react-router/serve 8.5.1, the current stable line; none of v8.5's unstable APIs (API-only mode, custom fetch metadata, route discovery) are used anywhere
reach.rationale: Every API in the app (loader, data(), Layout, Link/Outlet/Meta/Scripts, useNavigate/useSearchParams, ssr config, @react-router/serve) is long-stable React Router v7-era surface running on the current stable v8 release; grep for `unstable_|experimental_|future` across app/ returns nothing, matching the empty `experimental` marker list in the measured facts.

evidence: app/app/lib/api.server.ts:1-60 — all data access is wrapped in one plain-fetch server module; no framework APIs at risk of churn are involved
app/vite.config.ts:1-5 — bare `reactRouter()` vite plugin, no unstable RSC/view-transition plugins to isolate
app/app/root.tsx:2 — only core exports (Link, Links, Meta, Outlet, Scripts) used in the root layout
containment.rationale: Nothing experimental exists, so there is nothing to contain; even the app-specific data layer is already quarantined in a single `.server.ts` module that would survive any framework API change.

evidence: app/app/routes/pokemon.tsx:1 — `data` import is used solely to attach a 404 status to loader results, which the plain object return cannot express
app/app/routes/home.tsx:34-35 — filter state uses `useSearchParams` (stable) instead of any client-persistence API
app/app/components/MoveTable.tsx:9,52-54 — sorting is plain useState/useMemo, no framework novelty
justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used, so there is no unjustified reach; the few newer-but-stable utilities (like `data()` for HTTP statuses) each buy something the older stable form could not.

findings.issue: `isbot` is declared as a dependency but never imported anywhere in app/ (grep for `isbot` finds only package.json); it is a leftover from the default entry.server template.
findings.suggestion: Either remove the dependency or, if you want bot-aware streaming later, add an entry.server that actually uses it.

findings.issue: Loaders and components are hand-typed (`params: { name?: string }`, `loaderData: any`) instead of using the framework's stable typegen types (`Route.LoaderArgs`, `Route.ComponentProps`), so the app under-uses stable v8 conveniences rather than any experimental ones.
findings.suggestion: Adopt `Route.ComponentProps`/`Route.LoaderArgs` (typegen is already wired via the `typecheck` script and tsconfig rootDirs) to get typed loaderData instead of `any`.

summary: This is a deliberately boring app in the best sense: zero experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs, no future flags, and no unstable config options — everything it touches has been stable since React Router v7. It runs on 8.5.1, the current stable line (v8.0.0 released 2026-06-17), so it takes no version-currency risk either. The only adjacent observations are minor hygiene items (an unused `isbot` dep and hand-rolled loader typing) that involve stable, not experimental, surface.
